paragraph: Wallington's single-family market ran 13 sales over six months at a median of $745,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00 and a median of 28 days on market. About 31 percent sold above asking, which puts this in competitive but balanced territory. Well-priced homes are moving, and the good ones still draw competition, but sellers aren't dictating terms. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths, and prices spanned $570,000 to $1,275,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Two-families are the other half of this market, 9 sales at a median of $760,000, every one of them a two-family, typically five bedrooms and two baths. That tier is tighter: two thirds sold above asking, the sale-to-list ratio was 1.05, and the median was 19 days on market. Nine sales is a small sample, so read it as a firm tier rather than a runaway one. The monthly counts here are too thin to support a trend claim, one to four closings a month, so the six-month picture is the honest read. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the rental income of a two-family.
